summary: The device detected a near miss as an object closed at 4.2 m/s and was 3.40 m away at trigger, with no impact occurring. The video shows only a test pattern with no real-world environment or physical contact. The event was confirmed by sensor data but not visually verifiable in the clip.

sequence_of_events.description: Rear sensor R2 detected an approaching object with a closing rate of 4.2 m/s, time to contact of 0.9 s, and range of 3.40 m. A warning pulse was triggered on the back motor.
Near miss confirmed on sensor R2: object closing at 4.2 m/s, 0.8 s to contact, 3.40 m away, with no impact detected.
Video shows a large gray square appearing on the left side of the green bar in the test pattern.
Video shows the large gray square remains in the same position on the left side of the green bar.

clip_refs.observation: R2 sensor detected object closing at 4.2 m/s, 3.40 m away, with 0.9 s to contact.
Near miss confirmed with no impact detected.
Video shows gray square on green bar in test pattern.
Video shows gray square remains in place.

evidence.environment: Near-wearer conditions (indicative): CO2 612 ppm, temperature 21.4 C, relative humidity 38%.

hazard.energy_source: moving object (unspecified, likely falling or swinging item)

risk.severity_justification: The object was closing at 4.2 m/s and 3.40 m away, but no impact occurred — potential for injury if contact had occurred.
risk.likelihood_justification: The object was detected early by sensor R2 and warnings were issued, but the worker was not able to avoid it, indicating a high likelihood of failure in avoidance.

immediate.description: Worker did not take evasive action despite sensor warnings.
No visible environmental cues in video to indicate object presence or motion.

root_five_whys: Why was the object not avoided? Because the worker did not respond to the haptic warning.
Why didn’t the worker respond? Because the warning may have been insufficiently noticeable or timed.
Why was the warning insufficient? Because the sensor detected the object too late for the worker to react.
Why was the detection too late? Because the object was not visible in the video or environment.
Why was the object not visible? Because the video was a test pattern with no real-world environment.

corrective_actions.description: Review and optimize haptic alert timing and intensity for better worker response.
Implement visual or auditory backup alerts for sensor-based warnings.
Verify that test patterns are not used during active site operations.
